dominica.title: Flag of the Commonwealth of Dominica

colors.note: Background field; represents the lush vegetation of the island.
One arm of the cross; represents sunshine, the main agricultural products, and the Carib people.
One arm of the cross; represents the rich soil and African heritage.
One arm of the cross; represents the clear rivers, waterfalls, and the purity of aspiration.
Central disc bearing the sisserou parrot and ten stars; represents social justice.

desc:
- A green field with a triple cross of yellow, black, and white stripes, and a red disc at the centre bearing the sisserou parrot ringed by ten green five-pointed stars
- Designed by playwright Alwin Bully and adopted on 3 November 1978 at independence from the United Kingdom
- One of the few national flags to depict an endangered species: the endemic sisserou parrot (Amazona imperialis)
trivia:
- The ten stars represent the country's ten parishes; the ring of green five-pointed stars is unique among national flags
- The sisserou parrot is endemic to Dominica and appears on no other national flag
- The flag has been modified three times since adoption, including changes to the parrot's orientation and the stars' outline
